programme.title: The Australian Wars
programme.desc: European immigration increases in Tasmania alongside the death count as Aboriginal people resist occupation and colonists encroach on the best land.

programme.title: The Secret World of Haute Couture
programme.desc: Margy Kinmonth meets millionaire customers and world-famous designers as she explores the anachronistic but little-explained pocket of the fashion industry known as haute couture.

programme.title: Eurovision Classical Concerts
programme.sub-title: Lisbon: Gulbenkian Orchestra Plays Ravel's La Valse
programme.desc: Celebrating great music-making across Europe, a special concert from the Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, also featuring the works of Smetana and Debussy. Nicholas Collon presents.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Aston Hall in Birmingham, where treasures include some rare trading beads, memorable items from an Aston Villa legend and a collection of climbing gear from one of history's great mountaineers. Expert Will Farmer meets local man and celebrated poet Benjamin Zephaniah, who has brought along his own intriguing collection, and Fiona explores the Civil War-era history of the hall.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: Ancient tea-growing cultures, traditional seaweed-thatched villages, bird-filled wetlands, rare white dolphins, snake-infested islands and futuristic cities jostle along China's fertile eastern seaboard. The seaboard marks the front-line in the scramble for resources and space between 700 million people and a surprising wealth of wildlife.

programme.title: Raiders of the Lost Past with Janina Ramirez
programme.desc: Janina is in Crete on the trail of the millionaire who discovered the mythical palace of the Minotaur and the first Western civilisation, but who is now mired in controversy.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by guests Tom Baker, Alan Coren, Gabrielle Drake and Miriam Stoppard.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Arianna Stassinopoulos, Brian Redhead and John Bird. With guest musician Walter Susskind.

programme.title: The Joy of AI
programme.desc: Professor Jim Al-Khalili takes a look at how we have created machines that can simulate, augment, and even outperform the human mind, and why we shouldn't let this spook us.

programme.title: The Horizon Guide to AI
programme.desc: The BBC's Horizon programme began in 1964, and since then has produced films looking at computer technology and the emergence of `artificial intelligence'. The dreams always begin with ideology and optimism, only for this optimism to be replaced with suspicion that AI machines will take over. However, as the archive shows, throughout each decade once people have learnt to live with the new emerging technology of the time, the pattern begins again.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: The flood of funds into sculptural projects during the burgeoning British Empire unleashed a new, yet remarkably unorthodox, golden age. The greatest sculptors of the 18th and 19th centuries were mavericks who bucked prevailing trends - geniuses like John Flaxman, Francis Chantrey and Alfred Gilbert. Sooke reveals the technical breakthroughs behind their key works.

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Rugby legend Gareth Edwards and wife Maureen head to one of Wales' most popular holiday destinations. They arrive just as a heatwave hits turning Llandudno into a resort to rival the best sunny seaside locations.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth has asked the new vicar to tea and, in her usual meticulous way, she has organised the event down to the last sugar lump. Events take a sudden turn.

programme.title: Yes, Prime Minister
programme.desc: Jim unwittingly lies to the Commons about bugging an MP's phone. Sir Humphrey decides not to lie to the Privileges Committee on Jim's behalf, but then discovers that he too has something to hide.

programme.title: Ardal O'Hanlon: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: The story of a 1930s quest to find the origins of the earliest Irish men and women on the island of Ireland using archaeology. Ardal goes back to world-famous archaeological sites to see how Ireland had some of the most important finds in Europe.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: A Storyville documentary set in Bucha, Ukraine, following five protagonists as they attempt to rebuild their lives and come to terms with the legacy of war.

programme.title: British History's Biggest Fibs with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: Lucy debunks the `Glorious Revolution'. In 1688, the British Isles were invaded by a huge army led by Dutch prince, William of Orange. With his English wife Mary he stole the throne from Mary's father, the Catholic King James II. This was the death knell for absolute royal power and laid the foundations of our constitutional monarchy.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: This is the story of the men who built the canals, the navigators or `navvies'. They represented an `army' of hard physical men who were capable of enduring tough labour for long hours. Many roved the countryside looking for work and a better deal. They gained a reputation as troublesome outsiders, fond of drinking and living a life of ungodly debauchery. But who were they?

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Shire horses, lifeboat heroes and a rugby team who train on the beach are among friends old and new that Gareth and Maureen Edwards meet on a trip away to St Davids, Pembrokeshire.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Plants
programme.desc: It has long been known that plants can move, but recent studies have found that they can also smell, touch and taste, and have other surprising senses, allowing people to look at them with fresh eyes.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: A seasonal tale of how the Garden of Eden really was invaded not by a bad snake, but by one of the nation's favourite little birds.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: Bruce Parry treks into the high mountains in the tiny Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan, to live with the isolated Layap people. They are devout Buddhists and yak herders, cut off from the outside world for half the year by deep snow.

programme.title: Lowry: A Simple Man
programme.desc: A ballet celebrating the centenary of the birth of painter LS Lowry, first broadcast in 1987. Starring Christopher Gable and Moira Shearer. Carl Davis conducts the BBC Philharmonic. Introduced by actor Albert Finney.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis explores how, by the Wars of the Roses, castles were under attack from a new threat, the cannon, but survived into the Tudor era only to find their whole purpose challenged.
